Definition: to live, whether literally or figuratively; causatively, to revive
BiblicalUsage: To live, to revive, to come alive again is the word for God's power over death. The widow's child revives at Elijah's prayer, a dead man revives when he touches Elisha's bones, the dry bones live and stand as an exceeding great army, and Jacob lives seventeen years in Egypt.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the God who revives the dead child and the dry bones is the same God who gives me life. Revival is not a metaphor here: breath returns, bones stand, and the dead get up.
RelatedPeople: Elijah; Elisha; Ezekiel; Joseph, Son of Jacob
RelatedEvents: Elijah and the Widow of Zarephath; A Dead Man Revived by Elisha's Bones; The Valley of Dry Bones; Joseph and His Brothers
